Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Modeling Report

Overview

This report summarizes the construction, evaluation, and interpretation of a multi-fidelity, multi-output surrogate model. The report includes predictive performance, uncertainty quantification, and interpretability analyses for all model outputs and fidelities.

Model type: AdditiveVFM+RF+rho1 (AdditiveCorrectionVFM)
Fidelity levels: lo, hi
Outputs: park, currin, drag
Description: Example: Park and Currin benchmark pairs plus a 'drag' output whose low-fidelity level is pure noise. 300 low-fidelity and 120 high-fidelity runs.

Summary

  • Best configuration: AdditiveVFM+RF+rho1 (CV MSE 0.1733, chosen from 45 working candidates; runner-up AdditiveVFM+RF is 2% worse).
  • Highest-fidelity test R² is 0.737 to 0.992 across outputs.
  • Using the lower-fidelity data reduced mean test RMSE by 64% compared with an HF-only RF (0.2778 vs 0.7808).
  • Weakly related lower level(s): 'lo' (|r| < 0.5 with the highest-fidelity test outputs for at least one output), so they carry little usable information.
  • The 95% Gaussian interval covers 100% of test points; the predicted std may be conservative (intervals wider than needed).
  • Conformal 90% intervals cover 97% of test points.

Generated automatically from the metrics in this report.

Fidelity Levels

Data per fidelity level (lowest to highest). Mean and std are of the training outputs. r and R² come from a RF model trained on that level alone and scored against the highest-fidelity test outputs: a high r with a lower R² means the level is informative but biased (a multi-fidelity model can correct that), while a low r means it carries little usable information. The highest level's row is the HF-only baseline.

Uncertainty Metrics

These metrics assess how well the model's predictive uncertainties reflect the actual errors. Lower NLL and miscoverage indicate better calibrated uncertainty estimates; lower sharpness (mean predicted std) means tighter intervals, which is only useful when coverage holds.

Metric Value
Sharpness (mean predicted std) 0.72
Empirical coverage of 95% Gaussian interval 1.0
Miscoverage at 95% (|nominal − empirical|) 0.05
Gaussian NLL (mean per point) -0.509

Uncertainty Plots

These plots visualize calibration, sharpness, and other aspects of model uncertainty quantification.

Coverage Plot
Fraction of highest-fidelity test points inside the model's Gaussian interval (prediction ± z·std) at each nominal level. Points below the diagonal mean the predicted std is too small (overconfident); points above it mean the std is too large (underconfident).

Conformal Prediction Intervals

Conformal prediction provides distribution-free prediction intervals with finite-sample coverage guarantees. Unlike Gaussian confidence intervals, conformal intervals make no assumptions about error distributions and contain the true value with at least the specified probability on average (marginal coverage), provided calibration and test data are exchangeable.

Conformal Prediction Intervals (90%)
Split-conformal prediction intervals on the highest-fidelity test set, ordered by observed value. The half-width is calibrated on a held-out part of the highest-fidelity training data, so coverage is at least 90% on average when calibration and test points are exchangeable.
Conformal Prediction Summary
Left: share of highest-fidelity test points inside each output's conformal interval, against the 90% target (dashed). The grey band is the range expected from test-set sampling noise alone (±1.96 binomial standard errors); a bar outside it suggests real under- or over-coverage. Right: mean interval width, in each output's own units; narrower at the same coverage is better.
Gaussian CI vs Conformal PI Coverage
Empirical test-set coverage at each nominal level for Gaussian intervals (prediction ± z·std) and conformal intervals (prediction ± a quantile of the calibration residuals). Curves near the diagonal are well calibrated.

Sampling & Input Space Visualization

This section visualizes the distribution of the sampled input space and attempts to infer the sampling strategy used (e.g., LHS, random, grid).

Sampling Technique Inference

Inferred sampling method per fidelity level:
lo (n=300): Random. Monte Carlo test vs 199 simulated designs (Random p=0.185, LHS p=0.005, Sobol p=0.005; strata filled 0.61, centered discrepancy 3.41e-03) -> Random
hi (n=120): Random. Monte Carlo test vs 199 simulated designs (Random p=0.195, LHS p=0.005, Sobol p=0.005; strata filled 0.66, centered discrepancy 1.16e-02) -> Random

Appendix: Methodology & Notes

Summary of modeling methodology, dataset sizes, and miscellaneous notes.

Training data size: 297 across all levels (lo: 225, hi: 72)
Test data size: 30 (highest fidelity: hi)
Cross-validation: Model selected by Repeated 5-Fold CV (x3 repeats) on the highest-fidelity training data, then refit on all training data. Conformal intervals calibrated on 18 held-out points.
Random seed: 0
